title: AI-Powered Recruiting Platform
subtitle: Design explainable candidate ranking and interview support while recruiters retain the decision.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Discovery and the decision boundary
practice_prompts.hint: Ask the five discovery questions and say what each answer changes; state what the AI may and may not decide.

practice_prompts.label: Intake, extraction, matching and ranking
practice_prompts.hint: Trace the Senior AI Engineer role through both lanes, extraction, embeddings, search and weighted ranking with reasons.

practice_prompts.label: Questions, AI judge and human review
practice_prompts.hint: Explain the judge's rubric, the confidence threshold, what the reviewer sees and why nothing is booked before approval.

practice_prompts.label: Scale, privacy and fairness
practice_prompts.hint: Cover async event-driven intake, bursts, regions, deletion, audit logging and continuous fairness monitoring with owners.

rubric: I separated the resume and JD intake lanes and explained structured extraction as the line between documents and data.
I combined keyword and semantic matching and justified it with a labelled-set comparison.
I ranked on explicit weighted signals with reasons per candidate, and said weights alone do not prove fairness or job relevance.
I kept the AI judge rubric-based and provisional, named a confidence threshold for mandatory review, and kept booking behind recruiter approval.
I explained how async, event-driven processing, queues, caches, GPU inference and sharded vector search absorb a posting burst.
I covered encryption, RBAC, audit logging, deletion across derived data and continuous fairness monitoring, including the risk in learning from past hires.

editorial_review.evidence: Compared all 33 captured sections (7 intro, 13 interview casebook, 13 reference design) item by item with the previous casebook.md. The previous version was a compressed summary (about 2,900 words) that dropped or thinned: prompt-management templates, the 'Agentic AI' to 'Multi-Agent Systems' example, 'extraction lets later steps run on their own', the Module 04 'someone's career' judge warning, the chunking-by-format link, the annotations on all six regulatory sources, the three follow-up answers (reduced to one paragraph), the level-calibration framing sentence, several key takeaways and the closing 'decides at none' line. It also rendered the same security SVG twice, gave every figure a generic 'source figure 1' caption, and listed components ('profile storage', 'observation') that the source table does not have. This rewrite adds a numbered request-flow step, an AI-specific deep dive, an explicit trade-off close, three follow-up reveals and three labelled added constraint drills,. The brief keeps a scenario, a Senior AI Engineer trace and the task, because JD, ATS, PII, GDPR and EEOC need defining before the walkthrough. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): functional list naming only PDF and DOCX while the request flow takes LinkedIn and ATS records → the requirement lists all four formats, matching the flow and brief; 'past hiring success' listed as a ranking signal with no share in the 30/25/20/15/10 weights → taught as a deferred signal that enters, capped, only after its historical data is audited, keeping the starting mix at five shares summing to 100%.
